text:
alex: Quick check — planning a small TF change for prod/model-sts. Goal: reduce replicas from 5 -> 3, extend readinessProbe initialDelay, and add soft podAntiAffinity so we don't pack GPUs on the same host. Opening a PR in a few minutes, want to catch any obvious problems before I push. snippet below for the k8s bit, and the TF var change. :eyes:

alex: k8s snippet:
```yaml
spec:
  replicas: 3
  strategy:
    type: RollingUpdate
    rollingUpdate:
      maxUnavailable: 1
      maxSurge: 0
  template:
    spec:
      affinity:
        podAntiAffinity:
          preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
            - weight: 50
              podAffinityTerm:
                labelSelector:
                  matchExpressions:
                    - key: app
                      operator: In
                      values: [model-sts]
                topologyKey: kubernetes.io/hostname
      containers:
        - name: model
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /health
              port: 8080
            initialDelaySeconds: 20  # currently 5
            periodSeconds: 10
```

alex: TF change will just set var.replicas = 3 for prod/model and change initialDelay in the k8s_manifest module.

maria: :+1: What's the PDB/minAvailable on that STS? if minAvailable is 4 and you set replicas=3 we'll block the rollout.

chen: Also check any HPA or external autoscaler targeting that deployment. We had a case where HPA would try to scale to 6 and TF would fight it.

alex: Good call — PDB is currently minAvailable: 2 (we set it low on purpose for this one). No HPA on this statefulset, only a custom scaler for batch jobs (not for the model pods).

sam: My concern: some pods mount a local cache PVC and startup times are flaky. Extending readiness to 20s seems fine, but maybe bump to 30s for a day and monitor. If readiness is too short we get premature traffic and saturate GPU memory. :thinking_face:

maria: Can we do a canary partition to avoid cutting all at once? e.g., perform a rolling update with partitioned StatefulSet StatefulSetSet update: set spec.updateStrategy.rollingUpdate.partition=1 then let controller rotate 1 pod first.

chen: Cross-check alerting — if model latency > 1.5x baseline during the roll, auto-roll-back? We don't have automated rollback today but we do have perf-alerts in grafana. Can we wire a short-lived alert with a paging policy for the rollout window?

alex: I'll schedule a 30-min window and add a temporary grafana alert rule for the canary window. Plan from me:
- open TF PR with replicas=3 and readiness initialDelaySeconds=30
- add preferred podAntiAffinity snippet
- include k8s update strategy with rollingUpdate.partition=1 for the first canary pass
- create a pod annotation `rollout-owner: alex` so it's easy to filter logs/metrics

sam: Sounds good. For the TF change, consider using a var override instead of editing the module default so we can revert quickly. e.g., in prod model vars: `replica_count = 3` rather than changing module default.

alex: Yep will do var override. PR description will include rollback steps and the annotation.

deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: prod/model-sts canary rollout window 2025-11-02T14:00Z → 2025-11-02T14:30Z (triggered by alex).

maria: :thumbsup: please ping on the PR and drop the grafana link when alert is up. I'll keep an eye on pod restarts and PDB events.

chen: If you hit images pulling slowly, consider `prepull` on the canary node or temporarily bump imagePullPolicy to IfNotPresent for the rollout.

alex: Great — thanks all. I'll open PR now and tag @maria @chen @sam. Will include the small manifest snippet and the TF var change.

sam: :rocket:

alex: PR: https://git.redwood.example/infra/terraform/merge_requests/456 — description + rollback steps. Starting the canary at the scheduled window.
